test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A substantial limitation of the Human Development Index (HDI) is its inability to capture:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Social inequality and income distribution**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** was developed by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen** and was published by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in **1990**.
 
• It was designed to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to **people-centered policies**, using a composite score of three dimensions: **long and healthy life**, **knowledge**, and a **decent standard of living**.
 
• A major limitation of the HDI is that it relies on **national averages**, which effectively hides the **internal disparities** and **inequality** within a country's population.
 
• Because the index uses **arithmetic or geometric means** of aggregate data, it cannot distinguish between a country where wealth and health are evenly distributed and one where they are concentrated in a small **elite group**.
 
• Consequently, the standard HDI does not reflect **relative poverty**, **social exclusion**, or the **gap between the rich and the poor**, making it an insufficient tool for assessing **distributive justice**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI)**:
 
 
• Introduced in the **2010 Human Development Report** to specifically address the limitations of the standard HDI regarding **inequality**.
 
• The **IHDI** discounts the average value of each dimension according to its level of inequality; if there is no inequality, the **IHDI** equals the **HDI**.
 
 
 
• **Components of HDI**:
 
 
• **Health**: Measured by **life expectancy at birth**, reflecting the ability to lead a long life.
 
• **Education**: Measured by the **mean years of schooling** for adults aged 25 and **expected years of schooling** for children of school-entering age.
 
• **Standard of Living**: Measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** in **US Dollars**.
 
 
 
• **Other Exclusions**:
 
 
• Standard HDI also fails to measure **environmental sustainability**, **gender empowerment**, **political freedom**, and **human rights** protections.
